brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut — they keep 5.9% profit vs 3.8% for similar firms, and their cash is stuck for 104d vs 79d, so offer faster payment in exchange

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% price cut across rigid plastic packaging
priceAsk.target: Target ₹0.65–0.80/pc for 28 mm caps (currently market-fair at ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical)
priceAsk.basis: They keep 5.9% profit vs 3.8% for similar firms — there's room in their price. Market research shows modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (bringing us to 15 days after receipt) in return for the price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹22.57 L of cash for us, but it's worth that to them because their cash is stuck for 104d (vs 79d for similar firms) and they borrow money at about 12.19%

brief.financialLeverage: They're healthy — CRISIL A+ / Stable rating, they keep 5.9% of every ₹100 they sell (vs 3.8% similar firms), and revenue of ₹937.60 Cr. But their cash is stuck for 104d vs 79d for others, so they value being paid faster. We're just 0.59% of their revenue (₹5.49 Cr spend), so we're small to them — but their strong profits and tight cash cycle mean we can trade faster payment for a meaningful price cut around their 12.19% borrowing rate.

evidence.point: They keep more profit than similar firms
Their cash is stuck longer than similar firms
They pay their own suppliers slower than similar firms
Market asking price for 28 mm PP cap shows headroom
evidence.figure: ₹0.55–1.20/pc band, ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume

evidence.point: We're a small customer to them

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; revenue ₹2569.83 Cr, health B (65/100) — top second-source candidate

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers, pharma; revenue ₹1010.97 Cr, health B (73/100) — robust alternate for bottles/closures

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed moulded & blow-moulded packaging; revenue ₹701.17 Cr, health C (51/100) — broad capability across bottles/caps

risks: They're in the grey zone on financial distress (Altman Z 2.17) — push hard but don't tip them over; frame the ask around volume commitment and faster payment, not just a squeeze
We're only 0.59% of their revenue, so we have limited volume leverage — tie the ask to paying 15 days faster (worth ₹22.57 L to us, worth their 12.19% borrowing rate to them)
Market asking price for caps is already ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical — the ₹0.65–0.80 target needs higher volume or looser spec to justify, so be ready to commit volume
Their strong credit rating (CRISIL A+ / Stable) means they're stable, so they may resist hard — lead with the profit gap (5.9% vs 3.8%) and the cash-cycle benefit of faster payment
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: You're keeping 5.9% profit vs 3.8% for similar firms, and your cash is stuck for 104 days — we'd like to pay you 15 days faster in return for a 10–15% price cut that still leaves you ahead of your peers.
